proposals.Name: relocated_bindings_demand
proposals.Title: Relocate the Mug: Binding Demand and Binding Supply, Not Bank Content, Decide Whether Experience Retrieval Beats a Compiled Procedure
proposals.Short Hypothesis: On template environments the retrieval gain is procedure-bound because nothing instance-specific is both required for success and unguessable from priors; if the environment is edited so that the target object sits off its canonical receptacle (relocated PDDL initial state) and search is expensive (tight step budget), a scene-keyed retrieval residual over the best static prompt appears, but only when the bank contains a same-scene item carrying the new location, and a cached location table with one row per (scene, object class) recovers the same residual at zero uncached tokens.
proposals.Related Work: Measurement A on this node (k=3 retrieval +27/+32 net, unseen approximately equal to seen) and Measurement C (five static arms) are the starting position. RAP (arXiv:2402.03610) retrieves past experiences by current situation on ALFWorld/WebShop but never compares against a fixed exemplar set or a compiled prompt at matched tokens. State-grounded dynamic retrieval for web agents (arXiv:2606.04391) keys retrieval on page state but does not manipulate whether state matters. VTM-Nav (arXiv:2607.14514) reuses object locations across episodes in fixed scenes with no static control. SWE-ContextBench (arXiv:2602.08316) shows correctly selected related-task experience helps, with relatedness observed rather than manipulated. SGR-Bench (arXiv:2605.22219) attributes failures to site-specific state but never tests supplying stored procedures. The compliance trap (arXiv:2607.10608) shows agents adopt wrong retrieved memory; we use its stale-binding case as an exploratory arm. Archived ideas decorative_retriever (overlap observed, not manipulated) and abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (memory representation manipulated, environment demand held fixed) are the nearest prior ideas.
proposals.Abstract: Experience-memory papers report retrieval gains over no memory, but on template benchmarks such as ALFWorld the goal sentence reveals the procedure and a static prompt built once from the same experience captures most of the gain (Measurement A: unseen approximately equal to seen). We ask which environment property makes a query necessary and manipulate it directly rather than naming it. Binding demand is manipulated at two levels by editing the PDDL initial state of every evaluation game so that the target object is moved to a receptacle where its class never appears in training (canonical vs relocated), crossed with the step budget (50 vs 25); the relocation rule is deterministic per (scene, object class) so that sibling games in the same scene share the binding. Binding supply is manipulated by the bank: scene-matched fresh siblings (regenerated by the ALFWorld PDDL expert under relocation), scene-disjoint items only (valid_seen purged of same-scene items; valid_unseen replicates this by construction), and, exploratorily, stale same-scene items from the canonical games. Arms in every cell: k=0, goal-query retrieval k=3 (Measurement A), scene-query retrieval k=3 (query = goal plus initial room observation), type-conditioned fixed exemplars, type-agnostic all-six-procedures prompt, a random-type length placebo, a whole-bank arm (the type's 80 nearest items including the sibling), and a compiled location table (all six procedures plus one row per (scene, class) with the relocated receptacle, at most 274 rows, about 3k cached tokens). Every retrieval claim is reported as retrieval minus the best static arm on the same (game, seed), with uncached prefill tokens per episode logged. The design predicts a zero residual without demand or without supply, a residual of at least half the Gate-0 gain with both, and its recovery by the table without any query; each of these can fail in a named cell.
proposals.Experiments: 1. Construction: for each of the 274 eval games (valid_seen + valid_unseen) compute the canonical receptacle set of the target class from train (receptacles holding the class in >=5% of train games); relocate the object (both objects for pick-two) to a type-compatible, non-goal receptacle in the same scene outside that set, deterministic per (scene, class); edit the PDDL problem init; run the ALFWorld PDDL expert to verify solvability and to produce the fresh expert trajectory; drop and count games the planner cannot solve. Apply the same rule to all train games in the eval scenes to obtain the sibling supply (fresh relocated expert items). 2. Manipulation check (first, positive control): k=0 at canonical x {50, 25} and relocated x {50, 25}, 274 x 2 seeds each. Pre-registered escalation: if relocated x 25 does not drop k=0 success by >= 8 net vs canonical x 25, run one further level (budget 15 or +10 distractor objects in closed receptacles); if still no drop, stop and report the demand lever as inert. 3. Confirmatory cells (each arm 274 x 2 seeds, ~30 min): relocated x tight x fresh-sibling supply: goal-query k=3, scene-query k=3, type-agnostic static, compiled table, type-conditioned 3 exemplars, placebo; canonical x tight: goal-query, scene-query, type-agnostic; relocated x loose x fresh supply: scene-query, type-agnostic; relocated x tight x scene-disjoint supply: scene-query. 4. Exploratory: relocated x tight x stale-sibling supply (scene-query) for the compliance-trap direction; whole-bank arm at relocated x tight x fresh supply; per-type breakdown (clean/heat/cool vs pick-and-place vs pick-two vs look-at). 5. Cost: prefill tokens per episode split into cached (static prefix, vLLM prefix cache hits) and uncached (retrieved items), plus retriever wall-clock; accuracy-cost curve per cell. Total ~8,500 episodes, ~7-8 h at 20 episodes/min on two A100s (one vLLM replica per GPU).
proposals.Baselines and Ablations: Baselines (static, cached): type-agnostic all-six-procedures prompt (~400 tokens); type-conditioned 3 fixed expert exemplars (~430 tokens, matched to k=3); compiled location table (procedures + <=274 rows); random-type 3-exemplar length placebo; whole-bank 80-item arm (~11k tokens) as the no-query information-complete arm. Retrieval arms: goal-query k=3 (Measurement A retriever, unchanged) and scene-query k=3 (same embedding model, index text = goal + first observation). Ablations: supply (fresh sibling / scene-disjoint / stale sibling); demand (canonical/relocated x 50/25 steps); k=1 and k=7 for the scene-query arm at the positive cell; table with rows shuffled vs sorted by scene (lost-in-the-middle check); table restricted to the 20 rows of the current scene's classes (a cheaper compiled variant); second seed pair to check seed stability of the positive cell.
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (positive control) k=0 success at relocated x 25 steps is >= 8 net below canonical x 25 steps. Falsified if the drop is < 8 net; produced by the two k=0 cells. If falsified after the pre-registered escalation the demand lever is reported inert and the confirmatory cells are not run. P2 (no residual without demand) In canonical x 25 and in relocated x 50, scene-query retrieval minus type-agnostic static is <= +8 net. Falsified by a residual >= +8 in either cell (produced by the canonical x tight x scene-query cell or the relocated x loose x scene-query cell), meaning the residual is not gated by demand. P3 (residual with demand and supply) In relocated x 25 x fresh-sibling supply, scene-query retrieval minus type-agnostic static is >= +14 net (half the Gate-0 gain of 27). Falsified by < +8 net in that cell, meaning the reader cannot apply a location from a retrieved trajectory even when required (application failure, G7). P4 (binding-bound, not content-bound) In relocated x 25 x scene-disjoint supply, scene-query retrieval minus type-agnostic static is <= +8 net. Falsified by >= +8 in that cell, meaning the residual comes from non-binding content of retrieved trajectories (e.g., a search heuristic) rather than the binding. P5 (the query matters only under demand) In relocated x 25 x fresh supply, scene-query minus goal-query retrieval is >= +8 net, and in canonical x 25 it is within +-8. Falsified by scene-query minus goal-query < +8 in the relocated cell (goal similarity already keys the sibling through class-scene correlation) or >= +8 in the canonical cell; both cells exist. P6 (compilability) In relocated x 25 x fresh supply, compiled table minus scene-query retrieval is >= -8 net. Falsified by table < retrieval - 8 in that cell, meaning the reader can use a 430-token trajectory but not a 3k-token table, so the query is necessary at 274 rows. Exploratory (declared, not confirmatory): whole-bank 80-item arm is <= scene-query retrieval - 8 (the sibling is not found among 80 items); falsified by whole-bank >= retrieval - 8 in the whole-bank cell. Stale-sibling supply gives retrieval <= type-agnostic static - 8; falsified by retrieval >= static - 8 in the stale cell.
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: Primary outcome: task success on the same (game, seed) pairs across arms; nets in points; paired differences with a cluster bootstrap over games (1,000 resamples, seeds nested in games) giving 95% CIs; the +-8-net floor at 274 x 2 is the minimum reportable margin and all confirmatory margins (+14) exceed it; per-type differences (+-13 to +-15) are exploratory only. Fixed decoding temperature and seeds as in Measurement A; the same vLLM build, prompt template and retriever checkpoint in every arm; the static prefixes are byte-identical across episodes so prefix-cache hits are verified from the vLLM logs. Manipulation check precedes confirmatory cells; predictions and margins pre-registered in DESIGN.md before the first confirmatory cell. valid_seen and valid_unseen reported separately (unseen is the natural scene-disjoint supply), plus pooled. Prefill tokens per episode (cached/uncached) and wall-clock per episode logged for the accuracy-cost curve.
proposals.Preprint Collision Check: All queries run through tools/ideate2/s2cli.py (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers; both channels answered every query, hits labelled [s2]/[hf] as returned). (1) mechanism, last 12 months: 'instance-specific object location binding experience retrieval embodied agent versus static procedure prompt' --recent -> [hf] VTM-Nav 2607.14514 (cross-episode object-goal navigation memory in fixed scenes, no static control), FindingDory 2506.15635, MEMENTO 2505.16348, PIN 2410.18195, AutoAgent 2603.09716; none manipulates binding demand or compares against a compiled table. (2) closest named method: 'RAP retrieval-augmented planning contextual memory ALFWorld WebShop past experiences situation' -> [hf/s2] RAP 2402.03610 (situation-keyed experience retrieval on ALFWorld/WebShop; no fixed-exemplar or compiled arm), [hf] RA-DT 2410.07071, RaMem 2606.22844. (3) home: 'in-context example selection similarity versus random examples instance-specific information' -> [s2] SNAIL (NAACL 2025), query-focused submodular demonstration selection (2023), text-to-SQL example selection (2022); nothing on when similarity-selected examples beat random as a function of instance specificity. (4) home (retry): 'demonstration selection versus random demonstrations few-shot in-context learning' -> [s2] MarginSel 2506.06699 (+2-7 F1 over random on classification), [hf] gradient-matching many-shot selection 2506.04579, curriculum selection 2411.18126, RL visual demo selection 2603.26775, UniICL 2603.24690; all classification/regression, none in sequential decision tasks, none with a compiled-table control. (5) 'long context key-value lookup table number of entries accuracy degradation' --recent -> only [s2] DELTA 2510.09883 (efficiency); effectively empty for the table-lookup claim. (6) 'SGR-Bench state-gated retrieval search agents site-specific state' -> [hf] state-grounded dynamic retrieval for web agents 2606.04391 (retrieval keyed on page state, no static control, no manipulation of state necessity), [hf/s2] SGR-Bench 2605.22219. No paper found that relocates objects or otherwise plants instance bindings to test whether a query is necessary against a compiled table.
proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: PDDL edits must keep the text engine's object placement consistent (receptacle type compatibility, openable receptacles); some games will be unsolvable or planner-failing and are dropped with counts reported. The demand lever may be too weak for a 32B reader (mitigated by the pre-registered escalation to a 15-step budget or clutter); if it stays inert the study reports that ALFWorld cannot be made binding-bound cheaply. A failed P3 (application failure) leaves no positive residual anywhere, which is informative but not the headline. Relocation is a synthetic manipulation; deployment relevance rests on the analogy to site-specific state (SGR-Bench) and is argued, not measured, on a second environment (WebShop would need a day of setup). The table arm is small (<=274 rows) so the row count at which a table stops compiling is left to a separate ladder. Two seeds only; seed stability of the positive cell is checked but not a third seed.
proposals.Addresses gap: G6 (retrieval versus knowledge never separated: this design supplies the same knowledge as a compiled table and as retrieved trajectories under manipulated demand); secondarily G9 (whether stored trajectories improve action-taking rather than recall: success is the outcome).
proposals.Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'Measurement A: unseen approximately equal to seen, so the retrieved value is the type's procedure, not the scene': this idea claims that equality is a property of the canonical, loose-budget regime and names the cell (relocated x 25 x scene-keyed x fresh sibling) where it fails and the arm (compiled table) where it is restored without a query, neither of which the bullet states. Digest card arxiv:2602.08316 (SWE-ContextBench): this idea claims that correctly selected related-task experience is a binding-supply effect that a static row table replaces at equal success and zero uncached tokens, which that card never tests because relatedness is observed from dependency links rather than manipulated. Archived decorative_retriever and abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs observed overlap or changed the memory representation; here the environment's demand and the bank's supply are manipulated with the representation fixed.

proposals.Name: protocol_bindings_procedure_count
proposals.Title: How Many Procedures Before a Cached Prompt Needs a Query: Planting Protocol-Keyed Procedures to Manipulate Procedure Count in ALFWorld
proposals.Short Hypothesis: The residual of experience retrieval over a type-agnostic cached prompt is a routing residual: it is positive only when the reader's in-context selection among the P procedures the task distribution spans is worse than the retriever's selection. ALFWorld spans P = 6 and shows no residual; multiplying P by planting protocol-keyed hidden preconditions (P = 6, 24, 96, 288) produces a residual above a threshold P*, and a factorized compiled prompt (six procedures plus one row per protocol) removes it again, so the property that makes a query necessary is the size of the smallest compiled form of the procedure set, not the number of procedures.
proposals.Related Work: Enrich-Retrieve-Rank (arXiv:2608.22695) shows in-context routing over a capability registry collapses as the registry grows, measured by Match@1 with one small router and no compiled-table control. SGR-Bench (arXiv:2605.22219) attributes search-agent failures to site-specific state configuration but does not test supplying procedures. Mem2ActBench (arXiv:2601.19935) shows memory frameworks fail to ground tool parameters without a no-memory or full-history baseline. WALL-E 2.0 (arXiv:2504.15785) learns environment rules as symbolic knowledge by alignment, without comparing retrieval against a compiled rule set at varying rule counts. Toolshed (arXiv:2410.14594), ScaleMCP (arXiv:2505.06416) and Graph RAG-Tool Fusion (arXiv:2502.07223) report tool-retrieval recall at scale, not task success against an all-tools prompt. Measurement C on this node supplies the six-procedure type-agnostic arm. Archived optimizer_substitutes_for_memory_scaffold could not separate scaffold from content; the oracle-routed arm here does.
proposals.Abstract: A bank of 1,465 ALFWorld trajectories contains at most six procedures, so a 400-token cached prompt listing all six is a complete substitute for retrieval and the retriever's only job, type identification, is done by the reader. We test whether a query becomes necessary once the number of distinct procedures grows, by planting procedures rather than naming them. A harness wrapper imposes protocols: each game announces a random protocol code in its first observation (for example 'Protocol K17 is in force'); protocol k adds one hidden precondition to one key action of the task procedure (examine the object before heating it, open and close the goal receptacle before putting, issue look at a receptacle before taking from it, and so on, drawn from a menu of (trigger action, prerequisite) pairs), and a violating action returns the standard 'Nothing happens.' The protocol's content is never described in the observation; it is learnable only from experience. Expert trajectories are regenerated by rule under each protocol and verified by replay, giving a bank in which the correct procedure is keyed by (type, protocol). The number of protocols R in {1, 4, 16, 48} sets P = 6R. Arms per level: k=0 (manipulation check), retrieval keyed by goal plus protocol line (k=3), an all-P compiled prompt (every (type, protocol) procedure, about 35 tokens each, up to about 10k cached tokens), a factorized compiled prompt (six procedures plus one row per protocol, at most 1.1k tokens), the six-procedure prompt with no protocol knowledge, an oracle-routed static arm holding only this game's (type, protocol) procedure (the routing-free upper bound), a length placebo (all-P prompt padded to 10k tokens at R = 4), and a whole-bank arm where the per-protocol bank fits. The prediction is a threshold in R between 4 and 48 for the all-P prompt, no threshold for the factorized prompt, and no residual over the oracle arm at any R; a Qwen3-8B ladder tests whether the threshold moves with the reader.
proposals.Experiments: 1. Wrapper: intercept env.step; maintain per-episode predicates (examined(o), opened-then-closed(r), looked(r), inventory-checked, visited(landmark)); if the action is the protocol's trigger and its prerequisite is unmet, return 'Nothing happens.' without state change; protocol code inserted into the first observation. Define 48 distinct protocols as (trigger in {take, put, heat, cool, clean, use, go to}, prerequisite in a menu of 8 distinct prior actions) minus incoherent pairs; assign codes uniformly to games at each R with a fixed seed. 2. Bank: for each train and eval game and each protocol in force, insert the prerequisite step into the expert action sequence by rule and replay through the wrapped environment; keep verified successes; the retriever indexes goal plus protocol line. 3. Manipulation check: k=0 on unmodified games vs k=0 under R = 1, 274 x 2 seeds; pre-registered escalation if the drop is < 8 net: violations count as episode failure instead of 'Nothing happens.' 4. Confirmatory ladder, each arm 274 x 2 seeds (~30 min): at R in {1, 4, 16, 48}: retrieval k=3, all-P compiled, factorized compiled, six-procedure no-protocol prompt, oracle-routed static; plus length placebo at R = 4 and whole-bank at R in {1, 4}. About 24 arms, ~13k episodes, ~11 h on two A100s. 5. Reader ladder (exploratory): Qwen3-8B on retrieval, all-P and factorized at R in {4, 16, 48}, ~4 h. 6. Compile source ablation: all-P and factorized prompts written by rule (exact by construction) vs written by Qwen3-32B from the bank, at R = 16. 7. Cost: cached vs uncached prefill tokens and wall-clock per episode; accuracy-cost curves per R; note that cached tokens still add per-step decode cost, so wall-clock is reported alongside tokens.
proposals.Baselines and Ablations: Static baselines (cached): all-P compiled prompt; factorized compiled prompt; six-procedure no-protocol prompt (knowledge-free control); oracle-routed single procedure (routing-free upper bound, non-deployable); length placebo (R = 4 content padded with 264 procedures from protocols not in force, matched to the R = 48 prompt length) to separate routing burden from context length; whole-bank arm at R in {1, 4} (all verified items for the game's type and protocol, <= 80 items). Retrieval: goal plus protocol-line query, k=3; ablations k=1, k=7 at R = 48; goal-only query at R = 48 (protocol code absent from the query) to show the query must carry the binding; random-protocol retrieval placebo at R = 48. Ordering ablation: all-P prompt sorted by protocol code vs shuffled. Second reader (Qwen3-8B) on the three main arms.
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (positive control) Under R = 1, k=0 success is >= 8 net below k=0 on unmodified games. Falsified by a drop < 8 net (the reader discovers the precondition by trial within the budget); produced by the two k=0 cells; the pre-registered stricter wrapper is then used, and if the drop is still < 8 the study stops and reports the lever inert. P2 (no routing residual at low P) At R in {1, 4}, retrieval minus all-P compiled is <= +8 net. Falsified by a residual >= +8 at R = 4 (the reader already fails to route among 24 procedures), produced by the R = 4 retrieval and all-P cells. P3 (routing residual at high P) At R = 48, retrieval minus all-P compiled is >= +14 net, and the residual is non-decreasing in R. Falsified by < +8 net at R = 48 (the reader routes among 288 cached procedures as well as the retriever, so procedure count is not the property); produced by the R = 48 cells. P4 (not a context-length effect) At R = 4, the length placebo (10k-token prompt with 24 relevant procedures) is within +-8 of the unpadded all-P prompt. Falsified by placebo <= all-P - 8 (the degradation is length, not routing); produced by the placebo cell. P5 (factorization restores compilability) At R = 48, factorized compiled minus retrieval is >= -8 net. Falsified by factorized < retrieval - 8 (the reader cannot index 48 rows either, so the query is necessary at a row count of 48 and the property is table size, not procedure count); produced by the factorized cell at R = 48. P6 (residual is routing, not content) At every R, retrieval minus oracle-routed static is <= +8 net. Falsified by >= +8 at any R (retrieved trajectories carry value beyond the (type, protocol) procedure); produced by the oracle cells. P7 (exploratory, reader dependence) The smallest R with residual >= +14 is smaller for Qwen3-8B than for Qwen3-32B. Falsified by the 8B ladder showing no residual through R = 48 or the same threshold; produced by the 8B cells.
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: Task success on identical (game, seed, protocol assignment) triples across arms; paired nets with a cluster bootstrap over games (1,000 resamples) and 95% CIs; the +-8-net floor at 274 x 2 is the minimum reportable margin; confirmatory margins are +14 (half the Gate-0 gain). Protocol assignment fixed per R by seed so every arm sees the same codes; codes are random strings so the reader cannot infer content; the wrapper is deterministic. Same decoding settings, vLLM build, prompt template and retriever as Measurement A. Prefix-cache hits verified from vLLM logs for all static arms; cached and uncached prefill tokens and wall-clock logged per episode. Manipulation check first; ladder pre-registered with the threshold prediction (between R = 4 and R = 48) before the first confirmatory cell; per-type and per-protocol breakdowns exploratory.
proposals.Preprint Collision Check: All queries via tools/ideate2/s2cli.py (S2 + HF; both channels answered each query). (1) mechanism, last 12 months: 'site-specific procedures agent memory protocol state-gated tool parameters' --recent -> only MCP runtime/security papers ([hf] Agentao 2608.13574, Agent libOS 2606.03895, MCP-ITP 2601.07395, MCPTox 2508.14925); no relevant hit (empty for the claim). (2) mechanism, last 12 months: 'ALFWorld modified environment rules hidden preconditions procedural knowledge agent memory' --recent -> [hf] constant-context skill learning 2605.05413, Memp 2508.06433, self-generated in-context examples 2505.00234, WALL-E 2.0 2504.15785 (learns environment rules symbolically; no procedure-count manipulation, no compiled-prompt vs retrieval comparison); no paper plants protocol-keyed preconditions. (3) home: 'in-context routing capability registry scaling collapse tool selection number of tools' -> [hf] Enrich-Retrieve-Rank 2608.22695 (routing collapse with registry size, Match@1, one small router), Toolshed 2410.14594, ScaleMCP 2505.06416, Graph RAG-Tool Fusion 2502.07223, Re-Invoke 2408.01875, TRAJECT-Bench 2510.04550; none reports task success against an all-procedures prompt or a factorized table, none varies the count on one environment. (4) closest named method: 'SGR-Bench state-gated retrieval search agents site-specific state' -> [hf/s2] SGR-Bench 2605.22219, [hf] state-grounded dynamic retrieval 2606.04391, Harness-1 2606.02373; none supplies stored procedures or compares against a compiled set. Digest cards Mem2ActBench 2601.19935 and SGR-Bench 2605.22219 remain the closest work; no collision found on manipulating procedure count with a compiled-table control.
proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: Planted preconditions are synthetic; the claim to realism rests on the analogy to site-specific state gating and memory-dependent tool parameters (SGR-Bench, Mem2ActBench). The reader may discover a precondition by trial within one episode, weakening the manipulation (quantified by the k=0 check; pre-registered stricter wrapper). The all-P prompt at R = 48 is about 10k tokens and raises per-step decode cost even when cached, so accuracy-cost curves must use wall-clock as well as tokens; the length placebo separates length from routing but only at R = 4. A null at R = 48 (P3 false) bounds the threshold above 288 for a 32B reader and is reported as such with the 8B ladder as the positive control for the mechanism. Rule-based compilation is exact by construction, which favours the compiled arms relative to real deployments where playbooks are written by a model; the Qwen3-32B-written variant at R = 16 bounds this. Engineering risk in regenerating and replay-verifying 48 protocol banks (several thousand replays, cheap on CPU).
proposals.Addresses gap: G7 (whether deficits stem from the retrieval mechanism or from the inability to apply history, unresolved because no whole-history or compiled baseline is reported): the all-P and factorized compiled prompts are the whole-history analogues and the oracle-routed arm isolates application from routing; secondarily G6.
proposals.Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'ALFWorld has six task templates, so a bank of 1,465 items has at most six procedures in it' (inside Measurement A): this idea manipulates the procedure count that bullet holds fixed and claims a threshold in the count and its removal by factorization, which the bullet cannot state. Digest card arxiv:2608.22695 (Enrich-Retrieve-Rank): this idea claims the collapse of in-context routing is measurable in task success rather than Match@1, absent below about 100 procedures for a 32B reader, and removed by a factorized compiled table, none of which that card tests. Archived optimizer_substitutes_for_memory_scaffold and compile_dont_retrieve observed one procedure count; the oracle-routed arm separates routing from content and the ladder manipulates the count.

proposals.Name: binding_scope_leakage_ladder
proposals.Title: Global Fact, Scene Table, or Instance Replay: The Scope of Instance Bindings Sets How Much of a Memory Gain Is Near-Duplicate Leakage and Whether a Static Prompt Can Match It
proposals.Short Hypothesis: An experience bank helps on a new task instance only through information that transfers from bank items to that instance; the scope of the instance bindings (global rule, per-scene, per-instance) determines the smallest compiled substitute for retrieval (one sentence, a row table, none) and how much of the retrieval gain is near-duplicate leakage. At instance scope the gain exists only through duplicates of the evaluation instance in the bank and is linear in the duplicate rate with zero intercept; at global scope one compiled sentence matches retrieval and the duplicate rate is irrelevant beyond one item per class.
proposals.Related Work: Evo-Memory (arXiv:2511.20857) and ReMe (arXiv:2512.10696) measure memory as test-time evolution over task streams without reporting how much of the gain comes from near-duplicate tasks within the stream. EvoMemBench (arXiv:2605.18421) organizes memory by scope (in-episode vs cross-episode) and content, and finds long-context baselines outperform memory methods, but does not manipulate binding scope or duplicate rate. AgentCL (arXiv:2606.02461) builds controlled task streams with transfer-gain metrics, without a compiled-prompt arm or a scope manipulation. SWE-ContextBench (arXiv:2602.08316) draws related tasks from dependency links (observed relatedness). The compliance trap (arXiv:2607.10608) shows adoption of wrong retrieved memory. In the home literature, deduplication of training data (arXiv:2107.06499) and contamination analyses (ConTAM arXiv:2411.03923; rephrased-sample contamination arXiv:2311.04850) quantify score inflation from near-duplicate overlap for pretraining, never for experience banks. Archived order_randomized_leakage_audit audited leakage by order randomization (observed); Measurement A's unseen approximately equal to seen is the starting point.
proposals.Abstract: Memory benchmarks differ in what an experience bank can transfer to a new instance: a rule that holds everywhere, a binding that holds within a scene or site, or a binding that holds only for the instance itself, which the bank contains only if the instance recurs (sequential streams that revisit tasks). We manipulate this scope on ALFWorld using the relocation machinery (target objects moved off their canonical receptacle under a tight step budget, the cell where a binding-bound retrieval residual exists) with three relocation rules: global (every instance of a class goes to the same receptacle type in every scene), scene (per (scene, class)), and instance (per game). The bank's supply is manipulated as the fraction s of evaluation games whose scope unit has a relocated item in the bank (class covered / same-scene sibling present / the game's own earlier successful trial from a first pass present), with s in {0, 0.5, 1} at instance scope and {0, 1} at global and scene scope. Arms: scene-query retrieval k=3, the type-agnostic six-procedure prompt (no bindings), the scope-appropriate compiled static arm (one sentence per class at global scope; a row table at scene scope; none exists at instance scope), a 20-item bank (one relocated item per class) at global scope, a whole-bank 80-item arm at s = 1, and a length placebo. Retrieval is always reported minus the best static arm on the same (game, seed) with cached and uncached prefill tokens logged. The leakage index is the part of the retrieval gain removed by deleting scope-matched duplicates. The design predicts a compiled sentence matches retrieval at global scope, a table at scene scope, nothing but the duplicate itself at instance scope, and a linear zero-intercept dependence on the duplicate rate at instance scope; each prediction names the cell that can refute it.
proposals.Experiments: 1. Gate (pre-registered): the scene-scope, s = 1, relocated x 25-step cell must show scene-query retrieval minus type-agnostic static >= +14 net (the positive control shared with the relocation design); if it does not, the ladder is not run and the failure is reported. 2. Construction: three relocation rules applied to the PDDL init of the 274 eval games and of train games in eval scenes; expert trajectories regenerated with the ALFWorld PDDL expert; at instance scope the duplicate is the eval game's own verified success from a first pass by the same reader with the type-agnostic prompt (self-pool style, on-policy), placed in the bank for a fraction s of games chosen by seed. 3. Cells (each 274 x 2 seeds, ~30 min): instance scope: retrieval at s in {0, 0.5, 1}, type-agnostic static, whole-bank at s = 1; scene scope: retrieval at s in {0, 1}, type-agnostic static, table static, whole-bank at s = 1; global scope: retrieval at s in {0, 1}, retrieval with the 20-item one-per-class bank, type-agnostic static, compiled-sentence static, whole-bank at s = 1. About 17 cells, ~9.3k episodes, ~8 h on two A100s. 4. Exploratory: goal-query retrieval at instance scope s = 1 (does goal similarity find the self-duplicate); stale self-duplicate (from the canonical game) at instance scope; per-type breakdown; k=1 at instance scope s = 1. 5. Cost: cached vs uncached prefill per episode; the compiled-sentence and table arms have zero uncached tokens; accuracy-cost curve per scope.
proposals.Baselines and Ablations: Static baselines (cached): type-agnostic six-procedure prompt (no bindings, run at every scope since the games differ); compiled sentence per class (global scope only, ~20 sentences); compiled table per (scene, class) (scene scope; <= 274 rows); whole-bank 80-item arm at s = 1 for every scope (contains the duplicate; information-complete without a query); random-type length placebo. Retrieval: scene-query k=3 (goal plus first observation); ablations: goal-query at instance scope; k=1 and k=7 at instance scope s = 1; 20-item one-per-class bank at global scope vs the full relocated bank; stale duplicate at instance scope. Seeds: the s = 0.5 subset is drawn by seed and the complementary subset is run as a second draw to check that the linear estimate does not depend on which games carry duplicates.
proposals.Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (gate, positive control) At scene scope, s = 1, scene-query retrieval minus type-agnostic static >= +14 net. Falsified by < +8 in that cell; the ladder is then not run. P2 (global scope compiles to a sentence) At global scope, compiled-sentence static minus retrieval (s = 1) >= -8 net. Falsified by sentence < retrieval - 8 in the global-scope sentence cell (the reader applies a concrete trajectory but not a stated rule). P3 (global scope needs one item per class) At global scope, retrieval with the 20-item one-per-class bank is within +-8 of retrieval with the full relocated bank. Falsified by 20-item < full - 8 (a many-shot requirement per class) in the 20-item cell. P4 (scene scope compiles to a table) At scene scope, table static minus retrieval (s = 1) >= -8 net. Falsified by table < retrieval - 8 in the scene-scope table cell. P5 (instance scope: gain is replay) At instance scope, retrieval (s = 1, own earlier trial present) minus type-agnostic static >= +14 net. Falsified by < +8 in that cell (the reader does not exploit even an exact self-duplicate). P6 (linear, zero intercept) At instance scope, retrieval residual at s = 0.5 is within +-8 of half the residual at s = 1, and the residual at s = 0 is <= +8 (control cell; near-entailed by the split and declared as such, not a headline). Falsified by residual(0.5) >= residual(1) - 8 (superlinear: partial duplicates seed a search strategy that transfers to non-duplicated games) or residual(0.5) <= +8 while residual(1) >= +14 (sublinear: the reader trusts duplicates only when they are reliably present); produced by the s = 0.5 cell against the s = 1 cell. P7 (the whole-bank arm does not replace the query at instance scope) At instance scope s = 1, whole-bank 80-item arm <= retrieval - 8. Falsified by whole-bank >= retrieval - 8 in that cell (the reader finds its own trial among 80 items without a query). P8 (exploratory) At instance scope s = 1, goal-query retrieval residual <= scene-query residual - 8; falsified by goal-query within +-8 of scene-query in the goal-query cell.
proposals.Measurement and Noise Control: Task success on identical (game, seed) pairs across arms within each scope; paired nets with a cluster bootstrap over games (1,000 resamples) and 95% CIs; the +-8-net floor at 274 x 2 is the minimum reportable margin; confirmatory margins +14 (half the Gate-0 gain). The s = 0.5 subset is drawn by seed with a complementary second draw so the linear estimate is checked across draws; the same first-pass trajectories are used as duplicates in every arm at instance scope. Same decoding, vLLM build, prompt template and retriever as Measurement A; static prefixes byte-identical with cache hits verified from logs; cached and uncached prefill tokens and wall-clock per episode logged. Gate and predictions pre-registered before the first confirmatory cell; per-type claims exploratory; valid_seen and valid_unseen reported separately and pooled.

proposals.Risk Factors and Limitations: The ladder depends on the relocation positive control (gate); if no binding-bound residual exists on ALFWorld the design yields only the gate failure. Instance-scope duplicates come from the reader's own first-pass successes, so their coverage is limited to games the reader solved once (about 55-60% at k=0; the s ladder is defined over those games, reducing n and widening the floor to roughly +-11 net, which the margins still exceed). Global-scope relocation to a single receptacle type per class may be impossible for some (scene, class) pairs (receptacle absent); those games are dropped with counts. The compiled sentence at global scope is written by rule, favouring the compiled arm relative to model-written playbooks. Scope is manipulated on one environment; the cross-environment claim that a bank statistic (binding scope entropy) predicts the residual sign is stated as a follow-up on WebShop, not measured here. Two seeds only.
proposals.Addresses gap: G10 (how much of the benefit of experience retrieval depends on task relatedness or near-duplication within the stream, with token cost and scaling with memory size unreported): the duplicate rate and the binding scope are manipulated, the leakage share is measured against compiled static arms, and cached/uncached token cost per scope is logged.
proposals.Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'Measurement A: unseen approximately equal to seen, so the retrieved value is the type's procedure, not the scene': this idea claims that the seen-unseen gap is a leakage index that the binding scope moves from zero (global scope) to the whole retrieval gain (instance scope with self-duplicates), and that the compiled substitute shrinks from a sentence to a table to nothing along the same ladder, which the bullet does not state. Digest card arxiv:2511.20857 (Evo-Memory): this idea claims the stream gain at instance scope is linear in the duplicate rate with zero intercept and has no compiled substitute, while at global scope one sentence substitutes and one item per class suffices, none of which that card measures because the duplicate rate within its streams is neither controlled nor reported. Archived order_randomized_leakage_audit observed leakage by reordering; here the scope and rate of duplicates are manipulated.
